back: The main point or overall meaning of what is said.
notes: Listen for gist first, then for detail.

back: A specific fact: a time, place, name, number, price or instruction.
Words that show the structure of a talk: first, next, however, as a result, above all, to sum up.
Use the situation and the questions to guess what you will hear (times, places, reasons) so you know what to listen for.
Key words only, abbreviations (mtg, govt, approx.), headings and numbered points; fill in afterwards.
Who called, for whom, when, the message, the action needed and how to reply.
Speakers often give an old and a new time or place. Listen for not, instead, now, changed to.
Look for evaluative words: frankly, unfortunately, at last, I'm delighted, I'm not convinced.
the most important point, above all, I must stress, the key thing is.
